name: Dot
description: A survivor drawn alone, not from a pattern: a hooded figure at eight heads in a long cloak, sealed head to foot. Under a deep hood the helmet shows only a black visor with one cold blue line in it; the cloak hangs from a slate mantle clasped at the throat and falls behind the body to the calves, its hem edged in the last of the frost blue; tall boots come to the knee, strapped and buckled, and the near hand hangs loose out of the cloak in a sealed glove. What makes Dot Dot is the feelers: two dead antennae rooted at the crown of the hood, grown far past any other survivor's, that rise, bend forward and hang limp down over the face and chest to the belt — slate-grey, bobble-tipped, swaying when the body moves and sweeping, slowly, when it does not. No skin shows anywhere; the hive reads scent, and a body wrapped this tight gives it nothing. The dead pheromone core is socketed in the chest shell where the hive's would be lit, and the lash — a mandible on a cord — rides coiled on the belt at the hip. Drawn facing +x; the game flips it.

idle.description: standing under the hood, still: a slow breath through the chest shell that the mantle rides, the cloak's hem barely stirring, the near hand hanging loose out of the cloak — and the two long dead feelers, hung limp over the face and chest, swaying on a beat of their own, the only thing on the field that keeps searching

walk.description: a long stride under a long cloak: the knees bend and the boots come through the hem, the cloak is thrown back on every step, the near arm swings out of it with the elbow bent, and the two limp feelers swing forward and back over the chest a beat behind the shoulders
